newsitem.title: GERMANY: East Germany should avoid subsidy-dependence - panel.
newsitem.headline: East Germany should avoid subsidy-dependence - panel.

text.p: East Germany has made economic strides since unification six years ago, but runs the risk of becoming excessively dependent on subsidy transfers from the west, an independent government advisory panel said on Friday.
The so-called five "wise men" group said in a report that aid to the east was still needed, but priorities should be set to make sure that subsidies are targeted effectively.

"Economic policy faces a dilemma. Rebuilding needs massive support, but getting used to subsidies would hinder what needs to be achieved: the creation of independent and strong economic regions," it said.
Since unification six years ago, around 150 billion marks a year have been transferred to help reconstruct ex-communist eastern Germany.
Much of the aid has been funded by an unpopular solidarity tax, and Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government recently came close to collapse in a row over the timeplan for its reduction.

The panel said that subsidies should be structured so that they cease in the foreseeable future, even though there is a temptation to extend them due to a slowdown this year in the east German recovery.

Mistakes made in allowing east German wages to rise too fast without matching increases in productivity cannot be undone, the panel said. But more could be done to ensure that pay levels are in line with productivity -- as has been done in many companies which have spurned collective pay deals.
